correctness.rationale: All local geometric claims are proved on the true radius-one honeycomb: every hexagon point has exactly two or three covering disks almost everywhere; area of each unique active edge/path cell follows from mean multiplicity and motif density; direct circle arcs give four edge contributions minus two per deleted path. The degree identity gives perimeter quantization, and ergodicity gives all-q densities. Six direct finite-set area/arc quadratures and period-cell integration independently corroborated the formulas; finite sampling is not used as an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The 2007 Brown original deployment and 2015 Wang 2-cover methods are acknowledged as antecedents, while their inspected material does not give all-finite-defect motif identities, quantized perimeter, or Bernoulli area and exposed-boundary formulas. The closest prior research-record results are on geometrically different coverings. The known analogous triangular-lattice motif theorem is not a stronger instance; its disk-center graph, deletion threshold and coefficients differ. Priority risk from incompletely indexed reliability literature is recorded.

value.rationale: A natural full-plane doubly covered sensor deployment is extremely vulnerable to linked two-site failures, yet arbitrary finite failures admit exact metric damage statistics depending solely on two graph motifs. Quantized exposed boundary and a direct metric/combinatorial valuation are structural, not a numerical one-case enumeration. Exact all-q area and boundary densities are separately useful reliability observables and cannot be inferred merely from the number of sites or ordinary coverage probability.
